hints.title: Earliest Activity Identification
hints.text: Filter log rows to retain solely the hardware identifier linked to each participant initial participation record.

hints.title: Grouped Minimum Timestamp Pairing
hints.text: Isolate each participant first event date using grouped aggregation, then filter the source records matching both user and timestamp.

hints.title: Subquery Filtering Blueprint
hints.text: Select player_id and device_id where tuple (player_id, event_date) matches the subquery of minimum event_date grouped by player_id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT player_id, device_id
FROM Activity
WHERE (player_id, event_date) IN (
    SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date)
    FROM Activity
    GROUP BY player_id
);
```

variables: N: number of records in Activity table
complexity.notes: Aggregation and tuple filter execute in linear-logarithmic scan time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Grouping by player_id and selecting device_id directly returns arbitrary non-deterministic device values in SQL standards.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Subquery materialization isolates earliest login dates per account.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of subquery tuple filtering or window ranking functions.

solutions.code:
SELECT player_id, device_id
FROM Activity
WHERE (player_id, event_date) IN (
    SELECT player_id, MIN(event_date)
    FROM Activity
    GROUP BY player_id
);

import pandas as pd

def game_analysis(activity: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    sorted_df = activity.sort_values(by='event_date')
    first_logins = sorted_df.drop_duplicates(subset=['player_id'], keep='first')
    return first_logins[['player_id', 'device_id']]
solutions.approach: Pandas Sort and Drop Duplicates First
